paper_metadata.title: Toward Quantum Utility in Finance: A Robust Data-Driven Algorithm for Asset Clustering

experiments.description: Synthetic signed-graph clustering benchmark using GCS-Q on structurally balanced graphs with varying node counts and cluster counts, solved via D-Wave quantum annealing and evaluated against classical baselines using ARI.

algorithm.variant: GCS-Q (Graph-based Coalition Structure Generation) applied to asset clustering
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Terminate recursive partitioning when no cut has value lower than the sum of all edges in the current subgraph
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Start with all assets grouped together

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each minimum-cut subproblem in the recursive GCS-Q procedure is formulated as a QUBO over binary variables representing the cut partition
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize sum over clusters C of sum_{i<j, i,j in C} w_ij
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Recursive minimum-cut partitioning; no explicit penalty terms reported

problem_instance.description: Synthetic structurally balanced signed graphs designed to mimic financial correlation structures

dataset_specification.description: Graphs with continuous signed edge weights; intra-cluster edges sampled from [0.1, 1.0], inter-cluster edges sampled from [-1.0, -0.1]; non-uniform cluster sizes via Dirichlet-based stochastic allocation; evaluated across 33 random seeds

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Noisy-free synthetic generation; structurally balanced graph construction
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) over 33 random seeds for varying n and k

implementation_details.classical_solver: SPONGE, SPONGEsym, and PAM (k-Medoids) as baselines
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Correlation graph construction from synthetic signed weights; eigengap heuristic used for baseline k selection

speedup_claims.factor: O(n2^n) classical complexity for GCS-Q; adiabatic quantum process claimed to run in constant time
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical execution of GCS-Q / minimum-cut solving
speedup_claims.conditions: discussion section; ignoring hardware noise and cloud access overhead
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide a measured quantum-vs-classical runtime speedup; cloud queueing and internet latency dominate practical runtime.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly stated for the quantum annealing subroutine; discussion claims adiabatic quantum process theoretically runs in constant time
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(n2^n) for classical execution of GCS-Q, with O(2^n) from solving the minimum cut and O(n) from dynamically determining k
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: Per-QUBO solve times capped at 1 second; overall clustering of n=170, k=10 took over 10 minutes on average

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Penalty metric over business days in January 2025; lower is better
